source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 89: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 89. Backend, launcher, versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, topology, and exact blocked stage are unknown; measure them rather than infer them. Use an isolated authorized allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, set a finite watchdog, and guarantee cleanup. Record a run ID, host/rank/local-rank/world size, PID, config and software hashes, rendezvous/store endpoints and membership, per-rank collective entry/exit and last-progress times, stderr, transport diagnostics, and GPU/NIC identifiers. Verify each expected rank starts exactly once, membership and endpoint agree, all ranks enter collectives in identical order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping are unique, driver/runtime/backend compatibility holds, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology are healthy, and container devices, shared memory, ulimits, NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall settings are usable.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous-membership or selected transport-path defect prevents all participants from entering the same collective. Support it only when repeated matched trials show the same rank/path-specific missing or late membership, failed connectivity, or transport error and the symptom improves after one authorized correction; reject it if failures move across ranks or persist with verified membership and an alternate path. One run cannot establish causality.

Controlled experiment: run a minimal checksum-validated all-reduce with the same launcher, world size, rank mapping, environment, and bounded timeout. Randomize repeated trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while blocking unrelated changes. Compare default versus explicitly selected interfaces in isolation, keeping backend, message size, software, topology, and process limits fixed. Log success, timeout, rank failure, checksum/correctness, latency, and cleanup as separate denominators. A single-node pass localizes suspicion toward cross-host rendezvous or transport but does not prove it; reduced-world success does not establish full-world correctness. Test competing causes: collective-order divergence, duplicate/missing ranks, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access faults, driver/runtime mismatch, NIC routes/MTU/firewall/DNS, shared-memory or ulimit exhaustion, and scheduler/resource faults.

Mitigation and rollback: fail fast on incomplete membership, duplicate ranks, invalid device mapping, or unreachable endpoints; use documented interface selection and finite timeouts rather than indefinite retries. Preserve redacted logs, terminate only the owned process group after timeout, clean rendezvous state, and immediately restore the prior configuration if correctness, timeout rate, latency, or cleanup regresses. Promote a fix only after predeclared correctness and timeout/latency gates pass across repeated matched trials; otherwise keep the result provisional and require domain-expert review.
risks: The hang may instead be collective-order divergence, GPU/device/runtime failure, resource exhaustion, or intermittent infrastructure.
Single-node or reduced-world success does not establish full-world network correctness; finite trials can miss rare failures.
Interface changes and retries can affect shared traffic unless isolation, authorization, and bounded cleanup are enforced.

Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 98. Backend, launcher, versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, topology, and exact blocked stage are unknown; measure them rather than infer them. Use an isolated authorized allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, set a finite watchdog, and guarantee cleanup. Record a run ID, host/rank/local-rank/world size, PID, config and software hashes, rendezvous/store endpoints and membership, per-rank collective entry/exit and last-progress times, stderr, transport diagnostics, and GPU/NIC identifiers. Verify each expected rank starts exactly once, membership and endpoint agree, all ranks enter collectives in identical order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping are unique, driver/runtime/backend compatibility holds, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology are healthy, and container devices, shared memory, ulimits, NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall settings are usable.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific rendezvous-membership or selected transport-path defect prevents all participants from entering the same collective. Support it only when repeated matched trials show the same rank/path-specific missing or late membership, failed connectivity, or transport error and the symptom improves after one authorized correction; reject it if failures move across ranks or persist with verified membership and an alternate path. One run cannot establish causality.

Controlled experiment: run a minimal checksum-validated all-reduce with the same launcher, world size, rank mapping, environment, and bounded timeout. Randomize repeated trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world placements while blocking unrelated changes. Compare default versus explicitly selected interfaces in isolation, keeping backend, message size, software, topology, and process limits fixed. Log success, timeout, rank failure, checksum/correctness, latency, and cleanup as separate denominators. A single-node pass localizes suspicion toward cross-host rendezvous or transport but does not prove it; reduced-world success does not establish full-world correctness. Test competing causes: collective-order divergence, duplicate/missing ranks, wrong GPU visibility, topology/peer-access faults, driver/runtime mismatch, NIC routes/MTU/firewall/DNS, shared-memory or ulimit exhaustion, and scheduler/resource faults.

Mitigation and rollback: fail fast on incomplete membership, duplicate ranks, invalid device mapping, or unreachable endpoints; use documented interface selection and finite timeouts rather than indefinite retries. Preserve redacted logs, terminate only the owned process group after timeout, clean rendezvous state, and immediately restore the prior configuration if correctness, timeout rate, latency, or cleanup regresses. Promote a fix only after predeclared correctness and timeout/latency gates pass across repeated matched trials; otherwise keep the result provisional and require domain-expert review.
